edges.description: Altered beta-tubulin function perturbs neural progenitor cell-cycle progression and spindle orientation.
Altered beta-tubulin function also changes the position of migrating neurons and disrupts migration-dependent cortical organization.
A subset of TUBB variants additionally impairs the early stages of primary cilium assembly, a branch that is parallel to - not downstream of - the progenitor and migration arms.
Loss of tubb5 function derepresses Notch target genes that hold neural progenitors in an undifferentiated state, an arm shown so far only in zebrafish.

evidence.snippet: Furthermore, we demonstrate that the disease mechanism is not haploinsufficiency and that other patient mutations in TUBB affect cilia formation, putting forward defective ciliogenesis as a contributing pathogenic factor in a subset of tubulinopathy patients.

genetic_context.description: Reported disease alleles are heterozygous de novo missense substitutions. Haploinsufficiency has been tested directly and excluded: TUBB-haploid hTERT-RPE1 cells ciliate normally, and the G308S, E108K and E401K patient variants only produce their ciliation defect when overexpressed in wild-type cells - the signature of a gain-of-function rather than a loss-of-function allele. GAIN_OF_FUNCTION is therefore recorded here instead of the DOMINANT_NEGATIVE category used for TUBA1A and TUBB3. Curators should note the qualification the same work makes: E401K may act through a dual mechanism, with loss-of-function effects contributing to microcephaly while gain-of-function effects drive defective neuronal positioning, so this category describes the best-resolved ciliation and positioning arm rather than every phenotype of every allele.

nodes.description: A subset of TUBB variants impairs the early stages of primary cilium assembly. Because the ciliary axoneme is itself built from microtubules, the beta-tubulin lesion acts on ciliogenesis directly, without any basal body, transition zone or intraflagellar-transport gene defect. Patient-derived cells and gene-edited isogenic lines carrying G308S show reduced ciliation through altered microtubule dynamics and structure; knock-in mice show decreased ciliation in cerebellum and kidney; and E108K and E401K reproduce the defect. The mechanism is dose-dependent gain-of-function, not haploinsufficiency - TUBB-haploid cells ciliate normally - so this branch is allele-specific rather than a property of every TUBB variant. It is what connects this entry to the ciliopathy spectrum, and the patients carrying these alleles show ciliopathy-like brain features on MRI.

nodes.description: In a zebrafish tubb5 knockout, loss of the beta-tubulin isotype upregulates the Notch effectors notch1a and her5, which hold neural progenitors in an undifferentiated state: neurogenin1- and huc-positive neurons are reduced while sox2-positive cells increase. Pharmacological Notch inhibition with DAPT rescues the developmental and locomotor deficits, so the arm is reversible in that model. This is curated as a separate branch from the p53-apoptosis arm because it removes neurons by failing to make them rather than by killing them, and the two have different therapeutic implications. The evidence is zebrafish-only; see the gap_tubb_tubb5_notch_arm_human_translatability discussion.

nodes.description: Tubb/TUBB5 dysfunction affects neurogenic progenitors during corticogenesis. In the founding study, Tubb5 depletion perturbed progenitor cell-cycle progression and altered neuron position; in the knock-in mouse model, the E401K allele produced delayed cell-cycle progression, ectopic progenitor markers, and spindle-orientation defects. This progenitor branch is the main reason to model TUBB/TUBB5-related microcephaly separately from beta-tubulin disorders whose central skeleton is postmitotic neuronal migration.

nodes.description: A CRISPR/Cas9 tubb5-null zebrafish. Homozygotes die within two weeks post-fertilization with developmental delay, craniofacial malformation, uncoordinated movement, reduced locomotor activity, impaired photomotor response and increased seizure susceptibility. The model's distinctive contribution is a reversible mechanism: tubb5 loss derepresses Notch effectors that hold neural progenitors undifferentiated, and gamma-secretase inhibition rescues the phenotype.
